how_to_score: Score each criterion 0-4 using the scale below, then record the scores with `grade_records.py record-project <project-id> --scores 3,4,2,3,4,3`. The weighted percentage is the project mark; the rubric is the same for every project so the marks are comparable across the course.

scale.1: partial - some of it exists, little of it works
scale.2: basic - the core works, the edges do not
scale.3: solid - works well, edges handled, tested
scale.4: excellent - the standard you would show an employer

common_criteria.name: Functionality
common_criteria.prompt: Does the project do what the brief asks for? Are the required features all present and working?

common_criteria.name: Robustness
common_criteria.prompt: Does it handle bad input, empty data, missing files and edge cases without crashing?

common_criteria.name: Tests
common_criteria.prompt: Is there an automated test suite, does it pass from a clean checkout, and does it cover the core behaviour?

common_criteria.name: Code quality and structure
common_criteria.prompt: Are names, functions and modules clear? Is the code split sensibly? Any dead code or duplicated logic?

common_criteria.name: Documentation
common_criteria.prompt: Does the README say what it is, how to run it, and show the output? Are the public functions documented?
